bxps_recalibration.finding: SUPERSEDED IN PART — see midpointAssumption and intervalRederivation below. bXPS=220 was calibrated against the stepped xpCostTable model in Sprint 24. Sprint 25 switched to exponential 2.94*exp(stat/55) without re-calibrating. The exponential model's compounding makes 60-stat-point gains significantly more expensive than the flat table entries, so bXPS needed to increase proportionally. K was subsequently recalibrated from 55 to 47 via CV minimisation across 5 Grant ×40 observations (CV=3.2%). bXPS was then re-derived at 676 — the integral form of the XP budget equation with K=47 gives Grant Tackling 120 ×40 gain=65.7 (actual 59–73 ✓).

evidence.note: Grant data is actual before/after stats, not game-predicted range. Mid-range used as best estimate.

bxps_recalibration.rationale: Mean of 4 estimates: 495, 455, 414, 409 → mean 443. Initially set to 450. After K was recalibrated from 55 to 47 via CV minimisation across 5 Grant ×40 observations (CV=3.2%), bXPS was re-derived using the integral form of the XP budget equation: gain = C₀×K×[exp((stat+gain)/K) - exp(stat/K)] / ageMult. Solving the Grant Tackling 120 ×40 observation (budget = 40×bXPS/5 = 8×bXPS total, divided across 5 stats) gives bXPS=676: budget integral yields gain=65.7 (actual 59–73 ✓). All Dallas observations also validate at bXPS=676 with budget=4×676/3=901 XP/stat (MARKING 139 → 11.9 ✓ vs [11,16], POSITIONING 194 → 4.1 ✓ vs [4,6], AGGRESSION 189 → 4.5 ✓ vs [4,6]).

midpointAssumption.whatWasAssumed: Every impliedBxps figure in `evidence` was obtained by treating the midpoint of the game's displayed +lo-hi as the expected gain (gameMid/actualMid). The game states an INTERVAL. It has never stated where the expectation sits inside it, so the midpoint is an assumption, not an observation. Two of the Dallas rows (POSITIONING 194 and AGGRESSION 189) show the IDENTICAL interval [4,6] at different stat values, so the interval is far too coarse to separate them.
midpointAssumption.whyItMattered: The assumption is what made a point estimate possible at all. Without it each observation constrains an interval, not a value.
midpointAssumption.staleFigures: The per-stat impliedBxps values (495/455/414/409) and impliedBxpsAvg were computed under the SUPERSEDED cost curve K=55. They do not apply to the current K=47 engine and must not be re-used. The 'mean of 4 estimates -> 443' line in `rationale` is therefore not a derivation of anything; it is arithmetic over numbers from a model that no longer exists.

intervalRederivation.method: Each observation re-solved under the CURRENT engine (C0=2.94, K=47, geometric session budget, confirmed age and grey multipliers, Normal talent) for the bXPS that reproduces the interval's lower bound and its upper bound. No midpoint used.
intervalRederivation.verdict: All four observations are mutually consistent. They admit bXPS anywhere in 675-930. The value in the profile, 676, sits at the extreme LOWER EDGE of that band - it is admissible, but it is the floor, not the centre. It was obtained by solving one stat (Grant TACKLING) at its midpoint. CONSEQUENCE: every projection the app produces is at the conservative end of what this evidence equally permits; a value near 800 is no less supported. Do not treat 676 as measured.

divisorTest.question: Is the coach XP budget divided by the stats SHOWING ranges, or by the full category?
divisorTest.result: Re-solving with the Dallas Safeguard divisor set to 5 (full category) instead of 3 (rows with visible ranges) makes the four observations INCONSISTENT: they would require bXPS >= 1125 and <= 989 simultaneously.
divisorTest.conclusion: The 'rows showing ranges' convention used by coachBudgetPerStat is SUPPORTED - the full-category alternative is arithmetically impossible against this evidence. This is a positive finding, not an assumption.

bxps_recalibration.status: bXPS is an interval (675-930), not a point. Profile holds the floor of that interval.

role_whiteness_card_evidence._source: Four player cards, DarkVader FC, 2026-09-07. White/grey read by sampling the coloured key-attribute bar at the left edge of each stat row (DEF x=692, ATT x=1087, PHY x=1481; row centres y=515/580/645/710/775 at 2244x1008). 60 individual classifications.
role_whiteness_card_evidence._result: roleWeights.ts reproduces all four cards exactly. No change made to the role table.

learning_role_rule.finding: A LEARNING role confers NO white stats until it completes. Established roles only.
learning_role_rule.evidence: Darren Moore and SD Faye have the identical DC/DMC/MC role set. Faye (all three established) shows 13 white. Moore, whose MC chip is dark with a 2/50 counter, shows 10 white — exactly the DC+DMC union. The three-stat difference is entirely attributable to MC being incomplete.
learning_role_rule.code_status: Already handled. playerCardParse.ts sets roles = glyph.establishedRoles ?? base.roles, so when the glyph reader runs, player.role is established-only. The ML Kit text list (which does include the learning chip, as it sits inside the Roles: Y-band) is the fallback path only.

cards.name: King Alfie
cards.note: CROSSING white via DL. SHOOTING grey — no role here supplies it.

incomplete_role_cost._question: What white/grey differences exist purely because MC is at 2/50 rather than complete?
incomplete_role_cost.immediateStatTotal: +150 (2892 -> 3042), from the +50 T3 cumulative tier bonus applying to each newly-white stat at the moment it turns white
incomplete_role_cost.ovrGain: +10. Two independent routes agree: floor(3042/15)-floor(2892/15) = 202-192 = +10, and tier contribution floor(50x13/15)-floor(50x10/15) = 43-33 = +10.
incomplete_role_cost.ongoingEffect: Those three stats also stop costing 2x XP (grey weighting) for all future coaching and drills.
incomplete_role_cost.actionable: Completing Moore's MC role is worth +150 stat points and +10 OVR instantly, before any training.

cards.note: The control for Moore: same role set, all three established. SHOOTING, DRIBBLING and SPEED are white here.

cards.note: FINISHING white via AMC. Confirms Cieran Morgan is T4/MASTER and age 22, correcting the T0 recorded elsewhere in this file.

conflict_with_garry_mccluskey_record.issue: The garry_mccluskey entry records DC/DMC/MC as 12 white with SHOOTING grey. SD Faye has the same role set and shows 13 white with SHOOTING white.
conflict_with_garry_mccluskey_record.resolution: The card evidence takes precedence — it is a direct read of the game's own rendering, whereas the McCluskey whiteStats list appears to have been inferred. The most likely explanation is that one of McCluskey's roles was a learning role when that record was taken, exactly as Moore's MC is now. roleWeights.ts is NOT being changed on the strength of the McCluskey record.
conflict_with_garry_mccluskey_record.action: Re-scan Garry McCluskey's card and check whether any role chip carries an X/50 counter. If it does, that record's whiteStatCount should be re-derived from established roles only.

fan_club_surges._source: Direct in-game observation (Fan Club surge panels + training history), captured 2026-09-07. Values are read off the game UI, not inferred.

club_state.season: start — loyalty resets to 0 each season, so all surges begin inactive

condition_drain.charged_rule: charged = max(1, floor(raw)) — truncated to a whole percent, minimum 1
condition_drain.evidence: The drill pre-confirm dialog shows RAW; the training history shows CHARGED. Observed surge-inactive, 1 drill / 1 player: picker -0.75% (Very Easy) and -2.25% (Medium); history rows -1.00%, -2.00%, -3.00% only.
condition_drain.discrimination: Only floor-with-minimum yields exactly {1,2,3}. max(raw,1) would yield 1.50/2.25/3.75 and rounding would yield 4.00 for Very Hard; neither value ever appears in the history.

Easy.note: best value: 2x the intensity of Very Easy for the SAME charge

condition_drain.strategic_consequence: Very Easy is now STRICTLY DOMINATED by Easy — identical charged cost (1.00%), double the drill intensity. The old zero-drain strategy of spamming Very Easy is not merely weaker, it is the worst available choice.
condition_drain.open: Whether floor applies per drill or to the summed session is still unresolved. Also unresolved: floor vs round is inferred from the absence of any -4.00% row; a confirmed Very Hard single-drill session would settle it (floor predicts -3.00%, round predicts -4.00%).

chants.mechanic: A chant upgrades ONE surge chosen at random by one level. Chants come from tokens or the campus ball.
chants.expiry: Unused chants expire at end of season; loyalty also resets.
chants.odds: UNOBSERVED — campus ball probabilities not yet captured. Must not be assumed uniform.

open_questions: Whether the 1% floor and integer truncation apply per drill or to the summed session. Test: 2 Very Easy drills, one player, one session — per-session floor predicts -1.00% (floor of 1.50), per-drill predicts -2.00%.
Confirm floor vs round: a single Very Hard drill predicts -3.00% under floor, -4.00% under rounding.
Which loyalty threshold activates each surge (only 2 of 6 read ACTIVE at loyalty 10379).
Campus ball chant odds per surge.
Role Accelerator: base new-role point accrual rate is uncalibrated, so +20..+100% cannot yet be applied.
